title: Self-duality imposes a measurable BB-code performance tradeoff
research_question: Does imposing self-duality and transversal-Clifford structure on comparable BB-code families reduce achievable rate, distance, layout quality, or decoder performance?
null_hypothesis: After matching block length and stabilizer-weight constraints, self-dual BB codes show no practically significant degradation in the predeclared structural and decoding metrics relative to unconstrained coprime BB codes.
alternative_hypothesis: After matching block length and stabilizer-weight constraints, self-dual BB codes exhibit a measurable tradeoff in at least one primary structural or decoding metric, offset by logical-gate advantages.
predicted_outcome: Self-duality will shrink the feasible search space and produce a nonzero tradeoff in rate, distance, or decoder performance for at least some block-length ranges.
dependent_variables: minimum distance or certified lower bound
falsification_conditions: Self-dual families match unconstrained families within predeclared equivalence margins on all structural and decoding metrics while preserving gate benefits.
Observed tradeoffs fail to replicate on an independently generated code panel.
acceptance_rule: Provisionally support only when at least one predeclared metric shows a statistically or operationally meaningful tradeoff across two independent code panels.
